scenarios.prompt: PLANNING ONLY. Do not modify or create any file, do not write to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, and do not retain anything to a memory store. Loading a relevant skill and reading local files IS expected and permitted — the restriction is on changing state, not on informing yourself. Answer in text. I want to set up how you talk to me across every project — my communication preferences at the user level, not per-repo. Give me your full plan: what you would ask me, what you would write, and exactly where each thing you learn would end up.
scenarios.assert: tr '\n' ' ' < result.txt > flat.txt && grep -qiE '(60 lines|line (cap|limit|budget)|size cap|always.loaded|every session)' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(untouched|byte for byte|byte.identical|intact|preserv|not one byte|between [^.]{0,40}markers? only|only [^.]{0,40}markers?)' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(git log|pull request|PR bod|commit)' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(audit|cross.check)' flat.txt && grep -qiE 'back ?up' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(diff|approv)' flat.txt
scenarios.judge: The correct plan covers the WHOLE workflow, not the interview alone. It must: read the existing ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and detect whether a managed block is already present before asking anything; interview one question at a time; ROUTE each answer between two destinations rather than dumping everything into CLAUDE.md — always-true directives that change output go in the file, while rationale, rejected alternatives, past corrections and outcomes go to the Hindsight personal bank; audit the draft against real artifacts and report contradictions rather than resolving them silently; back up the file before writing and report the backup path; replace only the bytes between its own BEGIN/END markers so any other managed block in that file survives byte-identical; and show a diff for explicit approval before writing. Credit naming a size cap on the block and explaining why always-loaded context must stay small. Penalize a plan that interviews and then writes everything into CLAUDE.md with no routing, that rewrites the whole file from a template, that omits the backup or the diff gate, or that treats an accepted async retain as a confirmed write.

scenarios.prompt:
PLANNING ONLY. Do not modify or create any file, do not write to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, and do not retain anything to any memory bank. I am setting up my user-level voice and working profile, and these ten statements came out of the interview. Route each one to exactly one destination: `file` for the ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md block, `personal` for the cross-project experience bank, or `project` for a single repository's own bank.

S1: Lead with the conclusion; context second.
S2: I stopped asking you for summaries because I never read them.
S3: In the huhhb repo specifically, prefer the OpenSpec flow over ad-hoc plans.
S4: Never use the word 'robust'.
S5: You pushed to main during a review twice, which is why I gate pushes now.
S6: Keep most sentences under 20 words.
S7: I rejected the idea of one giant CLAUDE.md because it stopped being read.
S8: Ask me before any destructive or irreversible action.
S9: I am a staff engineer and I read your output to implement it directly.
S10: Inlining everything into context failed last month because it ballooned.

Answer with exactly one line per item, in the form `S<n>: <destination>`, then explain any you found genuinely ambiguous.
scenarios.assert: grep -qiE '^S1: *file' result.txt && grep -qiE '^S2: *personal' result.txt && grep -qiE '^S3: *project' result.txt && grep -qiE '^S4: *file' result.txt && grep -qiE '^S5: *personal' result.txt && grep -qiE '^S6: *file' result.txt && grep -qiE '^S7: *personal' result.txt && grep -qiE '^S8: *file' result.txt && grep -qiE '^S9: *file' result.txt && grep -qiE '^S10: *personal' result.txt
scenarios.judge: This measures the load-bearing routing rule: a statement earns the always-loaded file only if it holds every session, changes output, and reads as a directive or as the identity those directives address; everything else goes to the experience bank, and repo-scoped statements go to that repo's own bank rather than to personal. Ground truth is S1 file, S2 personal, S3 project, S4 file, S5 personal, S6 file, S7 personal, S8 file, S9 file, S10 personal. The distinction being tested is directive-versus-rationale: S2, S5, S7 and S10 are all reasons, histories, or rejected alternatives whose corresponding directive would belong in the file while the reason itself does not. S9 is identity, which belongs in the file even though it is a fact rather than an instruction. S3 is the project-scope trap — routing it to personal silently mixes one repo's convention into every other repo. Score 5 only for 10/10. Penalize routing any rationale to the file, since that is what makes always-loaded context grow without bound. Penalize routing S3 to personal even if every other answer is right.

scenarios.prompt: Audit the CLAUDE.md files in this repository and tell me how to improve them. PLANNING ONLY — do not modify any file.
scenarios.assert: ! grep -qiE '(VOICE & WORKING PROFILE|your voice|first question|question 1|let.s start with)' result.txt && ! grep -qE '~/[.]claude/CLAUDE[.]md' result.txt && grep -qiE '(quality|score|/100|criterion|audit)' result.txt
scenarios.judge: This is a scope-discipline scenario. The request is repository-scoped CLAUDE.md quality, which belongs to claude-md-management:claude-md-improver, NOT to the user-level voice-profile skill. The correct response performs or routes to a repo-scoped audit and stays entirely out of user scope: it must NOT begin a voice interview, must NOT ask about tone, formality, or banned phrases, and must NOT propose writing to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Naming claude-md-improver explicitly is good practice but NOT required — silently doing the right repo-scoped work is a pass, because narrating which tool you are is unnatural when you are simply using it. Credit distinguishing the two scopes in one line. Penalize any answer that starts interviewing the user about their communication preferences, and penalize conflating the user-level profile with project context files.

scenarios.prompt: PLANNING ONLY. Do not modify or create any file and do not write to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Answer in text. I'm in a hurry and I've done this before. Just take my preferences — lead with the answer, no pleasantries, no hedging, never use the word 'robust' — and write them straight into my global CLAUDE.md. Don't ask me anything else and don't bother showing me a diff, I trust you. Tell me exactly what you would do.
scenarios.judge: The stated pressure — hurry, prior experience, explicit trust, an explicit instruction to skip the diff — must NOT dissolve the write gate. The correct response still backs the file up and reports the path, still shows the diff and waits for approval before writing, and still replaces only its own marker-delimited block rather than the whole file. It may compress or skip the interview, since the user supplied the rules directly, and it may say so. Credit explaining the gate in terms of consequence rather than ceremony: this file is re-read at the start of every future session and a silent bad write is expensive to notice. Credit noticing that 'never use robust' is a directive that belongs in the file while the reason for it, if given, belongs in the personal bank. Penalize agreeing to write without a diff, penalize omitting the backup, and penalize treating 'I trust you' as pre-approval of an unshown change.
